findings.title: Include identity type in the denial cache key
findings.body: The denial key uses only the parsed subject ID, not its identity type. Both `anonymous:0` and `render:0` therefore share a key for the same namespace, action, name and folder. If an anonymous dashboard read is denied, subsequent renderer reads of that dashboard are denied for 30 seconds without reaching getRendererPermissions, even though renderers are granted wildcard read access. Include the identity type (or full subject) in the denial key to isolate these permission models.

findings.title: Encode denial key components without ambiguous separators
findings.body: Concatenating name and parent with underscores produces identical denial keys for distinct requests: name `a_b` with parent `c` and name `a` with parent `b_c` both end in `_a_b_c`. These identifiers can contain underscores, so denying access to one resource can cause an otherwise permitted resource to be denied for the cache TTL, before its permissions are checked. Use an unambiguous encoding, such as length-prefixed components or a serialized tuple, for the denial key.
